rationale: A is concise and readable, but it reorients by mutating the existing nodes in place: it appends the parent to the child and removes the child from the parent. Calling from_pov, or path_to, which calls it, therefore silently destroys the original tree. A second call on the same object would work against a corrupted structure, and _contains is re-run at every step of the path walk. B builds new Tree objects, so the original is left untouched, which is the robust, side-effect-free behaviour you would expect from a method that returns a new view. Its _find_path is a clean backtracking search. B's _reorient is somewhat denser and allocates more, but avoiding input mutation is a substantial quality advantage.
